title: Stalk tensor coordinates and invertibility of the pullback comparison
statement: Let f:X\to S and g:T\to S be scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme], Z=X\times_S T with projections p:Z\to X, q:Z\to T [def-pc-base-change], and z\in Z. Put R=\mathcal O_{S,f(p(z))}, A=\mathcal O_{X,p(z)}, B=\mathcal O_{T,q(z)}, C=\mathcal O_{Z,z}. The R-algebra structures on A and B are the stalk maps of f and g, transporting the latter along f(p(z))=g(q(z)); the ring map A\otimes_R B\to C is the unique map restricting to the stalk maps of p and q. Say f and g are stalkwise Tor independent if, for every x\in X, t\in T and equality f(x)=g(t), all \operatorname{Tor}_j^{\mathcal O_{S,f(x)}}(\mathcal O_{X,x},\mathcal O_{T,t}) vanish for j>0 [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. For P\in D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category], define the stalk-comparison invertibility condition at z as follows. For every K-flat complex K of sheaves of \mathcal O_X-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex] with Q(K)\cong P, put Q_z=K_{p(z)} using the module stalk functor [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. Apply the base-derived tensor cohomology model [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model] to (R,A,B,Q_z,C), giving its specified canonical map c_i:C\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}H^i(Q_z\otimes_R^L B)\to H^i(Q_z\otimes_A C). For every i\in\mathbf Z require (a) an isomorphism e:H^i(Q_z\otimes_A C)\cong H^i(Lp^*P)_z [def-pc-derived-pullback], and (b) that c_i followed by e is an isomorphism for every such e. This expresses invertibility of the canonical comparison independently of target coordinates: the canonical K-flat pullback-stalk identification is one such e, and postcomposition by any isomorphism preserves and reflects invertibility.
